lines.japanese: とくべつ空腹感はなかったけど、時間を潰す必要があったから学食へ向かった。
lines.english: I was not particularly hungry, but I needed to kill time, so I went to the cafeteria.

lines.japanese: さすがに期末テスト最終日の放課後、ランチタイム只中だというのに利用者は平時の半分もいなかった。
lines.english: It was lunchtime on the final day of exams, after school; naturally, not even half the usual crowd was there.

lines.japanese: 軽くジュースと菓子パンでも買って、どこか校舎の隅でひっそり食べようと思っていた。だけど、この状況を見ると不意に気が変わった。
lines.english: I had meant to buy a juice and a sweet roll, then eat in some quiet corner of the school. But the sight of the place changed my mind.

lines.japanese: 残務処理のひとつを遂行するチャンス。
lines.english: Here was my chance to settle another piece of unfinished business.

lines.japanese: 普段なら、近寄りがたいひとたちの不文律によって管理されているテーブル席の利用権だけど、これだけ空いていれば誰からもお咎めはないだろう。念入りに見渡したけど、警吏役のＨ組男子もいない。
lines.english: Ordinarily, unwritten laws enforced by unapproachable people governed the right to use the tables. With so many empty, surely no one would object. I surveyed the room with care. None of the boys from Class H who served as enforcers were present.

lines.japanese: 学園生活三度目の冬。こうして僕はついに、入学前のパンフレットで憧憬を覚えたチキンソテー＆エビフライ定食との邂逅を遂げることができた。
lines.english: The third winter of my school life. At last, I came face-to-face with the sautéed chicken and fried shrimp meal I had dreamed of ever since seeing the admissions brochure.

lines.japanese: 心地よい重みのトレーを手に、ソラ学カフェテリアを見まわす。
lines.english: With the pleasant weight of the tray in my hands, I surveyed the Misora cafeteria.

lines.japanese: ここに来ること自体は何度もあった。でもいつもは、自分のパンや森里君たちのブルガリを買うとすぐ立ちさっていたから、こんな風に、腰を据える場所をじっくり選ぶことなんて初めてだった。
lines.english: I had come here many times before. But ordinarily I left as soon as I bought my bread and the Bulgari for Morisato and his friends, so I had never taken my time choosing a place to sit.

lines.japanese: 奥のテーブルに高内さんたちが陣取っていた。目が合った気がしたので僕は軽く会釈した。でもやっぱり気のせいだったみたいで、とくに反応はなかった。
lines.english: Takauchi and her friends had occupied a table in the back. I thought our eyes met, so I gave them a slight bow. Apparently I had imagined it after all; there was no response.

lines.japanese: あっ、そうだ、あの席。
lines.english: Ah. Of course. That seat.

lines.japanese: ふと思いだして、僕は見晴らしが良さそうな窓際のテーブルに向かった。そこは、最上級生になって学食を使えるようになった森里君が、四月からよく座っていた場所だ。
lines.english: The memory came to me, and I headed for a table by the window that seemed to offer a fine view. Ever since April, when becoming a senior had granted him the right to use the cafeteria, Morisato often sat there.

lines.japanese: テーブルにトレーを置くと、箸を取るより先にまず硬い椅子の感触を愉しんだ。深く腰掛けて、森里君がそうしてたみたいに片膝を立てる。
lines.english: I set down my tray. Before taking up my chopsticks, I savored the hardness of the chair. I settled deep into it and raised one knee, the way Morisato did.

lines.japanese: 廊下の窓から見るのとは違う新鮮な眺望。ブラウンソースのかかった白い鶏肉。自販機でジュースをふたつ買っていく一年生。なんだか自分がちょっとだけ偉くなったみたいだ。
lines.english: A fresh prospect, different from the view through a hallway window. White chicken under brown sauce. A first-year student buying two juices from a vending machine. Somehow I felt a little more important.

lines.japanese: 「いただきます」
lines.english: “Thanks for the food.”

lines.japanese: 僕は脚を下ろして割り箸を割った。カットされたチキンを一片、口に入れる。つるっとした舌触りに柔かな歯ごたえ。安物ながら値段以上の味わいがあった。
lines.english: I put my leg down and split my chopsticks. I popped a piece of cut chicken into my mouth. Smooth on my tongue, tender when I bit down. Cheap, but better than the price suggested.

lines.japanese: 続いてエビフライ……しかし、そこで僕は小さなミスを犯した。中濃ソースを手にしたつもりが、容器から出てきたのは粘度のない真っ黒な液体だった。
lines.english: Next came the fried shrimp… and there I made a small mistake. I thought I had picked up the thick brown sauce. Instead, a thin, jet-black liquid came out of the bottle.
“…What?”

lines.japanese: ぐっと目を近づけてきつね色の衣にかかった香りを確かめようとしたとき、はるか柳木原の街並とは反対側から、騒々しい声と足音の一団が近付いてきた。
lines.english: I leaned in to smell whatever had landed on the golden breading. Just then, from the side opposite the distant streets of Yanagihara, a noisy mass of voices and footsteps approached.

lines.japanese: Ｈ組の男子たちだ。
lines.english: The boys from Class H.

lines.japanese: 彼らは他の空席なんて見えていないかのように、まっすぐ僕のテーブルへやってきた。大きな声で、笑ったり誰かの悪口を言ったりしながら。
lines.english: As though none of the other empty seats existed, they came straight to my table, laughing loudly and badmouthing people as they came.

lines.japanese: がた、がたがたがたっ。
lines.english: Clatter. Clatter-clatter-clatter.

lines.japanese: 同じテーブルで、すぐ隣りで、彼らは椅子を引き次々に腰を落とす。砂埃を巻きあげそうな勢いだ。僕は食べ物に目を落としながら、可能なかぎり自分の椅子を窓際に寄せた。
lines.english: At my table, immediately beside me, they dragged out chairs and dropped into them one after another, with enough force to raise a cloud of dust. Keeping my eyes on my food, I edged my chair as close to the window as I could.

lines.japanese: それから急いで昼食の掃討にかかった。向かいの席と隣りの席で、食事どきに相応しくない下品な冗談が飛びかう。僕のコンソメスープの水面に、かすかな点が降った。どちらかの唾が飛んだみたいだ。
lines.english: Then I began the urgent work of annihilating my lunch. Across from me and beside me, vulgar jokes unfit for any meal flew back and forth. Tiny specks rained upon the surface of my consommé. Someone’s spit, it seemed.

lines.japanese: 「つか、なにヨユーこいて休んでンだよ、意味わかんねーわ。追試だとペナ付いて、元のより難しくなんじゃん。あいつもう終わってね？」
lines.english: “Seriously, what’s he doing taking it easy? Makes no damn sense. You get penalized on the makeup exam, right? It’s harder than the original. Isn’t he completely screwed?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それ以前に。テストとか以前に。あいつ卒業する気あんのかよ」
lines.english: “Forget the exams. Does he even plan on graduating?”

lines.japanese: 「まーしかし、俺らもそんなひとのこた言えねーけど、まぁーあいつの落ちたこと落ちたこと。一年とき、俺らん中じゃいちばんアタマ良かったのにな。いまじゃメンヘル通いだろ」
lines.english: “Well, we can’t exactly talk, but damn, has that guy fallen. Back in first year he was the smartest one of us. Now he’s always running off to the shrink.”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱアレでしょ、あいつは。なんか妙なあの、ギャングだかゾクだか、そんなヤベー連中とツルみだしてから。ほんと、いまどきあーゆーガチな連中と付きあっちゃダメでしょー」
lines.english: “It’s gotta be that, right? He started hanging around with that weird gang, or biker crew, or whatever they are. Real bad news. You seriously shouldn’t get mixed up with hardcore guys like that these days.”

lines.japanese: 「まァ、虎の威を借りたくて必死だったんだろ。あいつホレ、一年ときのあの一件以来、すっかりハブられちゃって。二年のころには相当ナメられてたし」
lines.english: “Guess he was desperate to act tough with a tiger at his back. You know how he got completely frozen out after that thing in first year. By second year nobody had any respect for him.”

lines.japanese: 「ぶはは、他人事みてーに言うなよ」
lines.english: “Bwahaha! Don’t say it like you had nothing to do with it.”

lines.japanese: 「でもあいつ、ある意味天才だぜ、あぶれ者の天才。だって、ソラ学の坊ちゃんたちとウマ合わねーから俺らみたいのと一緒してたのに、結局そこでも浮いちゃったわけじゃん」
lines.english: “But the guy’s a genius in his own way. A genius at being an outcast. He couldn’t get along with the rich kids at Misora, so he hung around with people like us—and then he managed to become an outsider here too.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、なんかそういう話あったよな。たとえ話でさ。なんだっけホラ、鳥の群れにもケモノの群れにも入れなかった、中途半端な動物の話？」
lines.english: “Oh yeah, there was some story like that. A fable or something. What was it again? You know, about some in-between animal that couldn’t fit in with either the birds or the beasts?”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。すげえな和馬。コウモリ和馬じゃん」
lines.english: “No way. That’s brilliant, Kazuma. Kazuma the Bat!”

lines.japanese: 「バカおまえ、名前出すなよ。チクられたらゾクの皆さんがブンブンいわして校門来んぜ」
lines.english: “Idiot, don’t say his name. If somebody snitches, his biker friends will come roaring up to the school gates.”

lines.japanese: 僕は下を向いたまま、夢中で食事に取りくんでいた。でも不意にあからさまな視線を感じて、さらに緊張が増した。
lines.english: I kept my head down and devoted myself to eating. Then I felt an unmistakable stare upon me, and the tension wound tighter.
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: 掴みそこねたエビフライが割り箸からこぼれてテーブルに落ち、そこでも弾かれて足元に転がった。
lines.english: The fried shrimp slipped from my chopsticks, struck the tabletop, bounced from that as well, and rolled to my feet.

lines.japanese: 僕はそっと椅子を引いて、落ちたエビフライを皿に戻した。それを見ていたＨ組のひとたちが、何人かで目配せを交わしてくぐもった笑い声をあげた。
lines.english: I quietly drew back my chair and returned the fallen shrimp to my plate. Several of the boys from Class H, who had been watching, exchanged glances and broke into muffled laughter.

lines.japanese: 見られているのは分かっていたけど、僕は気付かない振りをして拾ったものを口に入れた。
lines.english: I knew they were watching. Pretending not to notice, I put what I had retrieved into my mouth.

lines.japanese: 三年越しのエビフライは醤油の味がした。でも悪くはなかった。むしろ僕は好きだ。ソースをかけるなんて、当たりまえすぎて面白みがない。
lines.english: The fried shrimp I had waited three years to taste was flavored with soy sauce. It was not bad. In fact, I liked it. Pouring sauce over it would have been too obvious to be interesting.

lines.japanese: 窮屈な食事を終えて──終わりにして──僕は席を立った。コンソメスープはとても飲む気になれず、器に口を付けさえしなかった。
lines.english: I finished—put an end to—the cramped meal and rose. I could not bring myself to drink the consommé; I never once put the bowl to my lips.

lines.japanese: 最後に一瞬、窓の外を眺めた。もう二度と見ることはないだろう、この場所からの白い空。
lines.english: At the end, I looked out the window for a single moment. The white sky as seen from this place, which I would surely never see again.

lines.japanese: やっぱり昼食は、パンと紅茶と校舎の隅だ。
lines.english: Yeah. Lunch was bread, tea, and a corner of the school after all.
